doc: Payload budgets per consumer profile (kemiller2002/limen#19). Each budget is the measured baseline plus 10%, rounded up to a whole KiB; test/bench-size.test.ts fails when a profile exceeds its budget or loads a forbidden module. Raising a budget needs its own work item saying what grew and why; lowering one after an optimization is encouraged.

history.change: Re-baselined every profile after the binding security policy (src/kernel/binding-policy.ts, kemiller2002/limen#18): each profile that loads the kernel grew by about 2.1 KB gzip (6.8 KB raw). kernel-only and kernel-with-handles exceeded their budgets; the rest had not, but are re-baselined by the same rule so every budget keeps 10% headroom over what ships.
Added kernel-with-focus (kemiller2002/limen#23): the focus pack adds 3876 bytes gzip over kernel-only, and only to applications that register it.
Added kernel-with-schedule (kemiller2002/limen#24): the scheduling pack adds 2689 bytes gzip over the kernel, and only to applications that register it.

profiles.name: minimal-consumer
profiles.doc: What examples/minimal (the copy shipped in the package) loads: the package root. It carries the reference email engine and federation, which a consumer never registers — see docs/27-performance-baseline.md.

profiles.name: kernel-only
profiles.doc: The ./kernel subpath: BrowserKernel and what it needs, nothing else.

profiles.name: kernel-with-handles
profiles.doc: A representative optional set: the kernel plus capability-support's handle table, the library every handle-returning pack imports.

profiles.name: kernel-with-dotnet-host
profiles.doc: The kernel plus the .NET WebAssembly host adapter (F# and C# guests), excluding the .NET runtime itself.

profiles.name: kernel-with-raw-host
profiles.doc: The kernel plus the raw WebAssembly host adapter (Rust guest), excluding the .wasm module.

profiles.name: kernel-with-focus
profiles.doc: The kernel plus the focus, selection and scroll capability pack (./capabilities/focus), as an application that registers it loads them.

profiles.name: kernel-with-schedule
profiles.doc: The kernel plus the scheduling capability pack (./capabilities/schedule), as an application that registers it loads them.
